Alice — thanks, adding the requested breakdown below (summary first, then assumptions). Full numbers and model-by-model tabs are in the attached spreadsheet.

High-level benchmark (effective $ / 1M tokens) — baseline profile ~ 340 tokens per request (prompt+completion):
- OpenAI (gpt-4.x family equivalent, public API, PAYG): ~$42 / 1M tokens (includes average retry/latency overhead we observed at scale).
- Anthropic (claude-like, public API, PAYG): ~$36 / 1M tokens.
- Open-model hosts (typical managed host + single-tenant GPU, conservative ops overhead): $18–$28 / 1M tokens depending on instance efficiency, batching, and quantization.
- Redwood hosted (PAYG, optimized runtime): ~$30 / 1M tokens (we assume standard FP16 + intelligent batching/caching).
- Redwood dedicated/committed (reserved capacity with 12mo commit, optimized quantization & batching): $12–$20 / 1M tokens depending on commitment level and model quantization (int8/ptq).

Key assumptions and levers that drive these numbers:
- Token mix: the profile above assumes 35% prompt tokens / 65% completion tokens. More asymmetric workloads (short prompts, long completions) shift unit economics.
- Batching & latency SLOs: continuous batching reduces per-token compute; we conservatively modeled a 1.6x efficiency gain for dedicated fleets vs PAYG.
- KV/prefix cache hit rates: high cache hit (50%+) lowers average compute per request for session-based apps.
- Quantization: int8/ptq can reduce GPU memory footprint and increase throughput; we modeled a 20–35% cost improvement when safely applicable.
- Overheads: includes network egress, orchestration, model loading, and expected retry/timeout overhead for public hosted APIs.

Notes on comparability: public API prices from OpenAI/Anthropic are list prices; effective costs at scale include retries, partial failures, and differences in latency that affect throughput. Managed open-model hosting varies widely by provider; the spreadsheet shows two real-host examples (HostA, HostB) we benchmarked.

Attached: redwood_vs_hosts_pricing_table.xlsx (tabs: summary, per-model assumptions, host-comparison, sensitivity-analysis).

Recommended next steps:
1) If you can share a small anonymized sample of 500 request traces (prompt and completion token counts), we can run an exact cost projection and recommend the optimal reserved tier.
2) If committed pricing looks attractive, we can put together a 12-month reserved proposal with staged commit sizes (pilot -> scale).
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk the spreadsheet and proposed deal structure.

Marissa, looping you in for committed/dedicated pricing approval on the upper ranges — can you confirm if a $12/1M floor is feasible for a 12mo $X commit?
